BudgetWise: .NET 8 ASP.NET Core Web API + React/TypeScript/Vite/Tailwind personal-finance workshop app.

C#: PascalCase types/methods/properties, camelCase locals/parameters; descriptive names, focused methods, composition, C# 12 where appropriate, `var` when obvious, `using` inside namespaces. Use constructor DI and appropriate service lifetimes; consistent minimal APIs or controllers; REST nouns/HTTP actions; typed results; validation, middleware, separate immutable `record` DTOs, explicit mapping. XML-doc public APIs with applicable `<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, `<exception>`; comments explain why; mark incomplete work `// TODO:` with a clear description.

Frontend: strict TypeScript, React hooks/functional components, reusable focused components, Tailwind (no inline styles), semantic accessible HTML, ARIA and keyboard navigation. Document TypeScript APIs with JSDoc.

Tests: xUnit, React Testing Library, AAA, descriptive `MethodName_WhenCondition_ThenExpectedResult`; integration tests with `WebApplicationFactory<T>`; mock external dependencies/API calls (MSW or similar); cover success, failure, edge/boundary cases, accessibility, and user interactions (not implementation details); use Testing Library `screen`. Test new features.

API: appropriate GET/POST/PUT/DELETE, status codes, plural resource paths, IDs in path variables, filters/search in query parameters, DTOs, validation, meaningful errors, camelCase JSON, Content-Type headers.

Data: in-memory collections for development/tests; realistic `MockData` in `Data/MockData.cs`; thread safety where needed; property initialization, navigation properties, nullable references and `required` for mandatory properties.

Check existing patterns; follow ASP.NET and frontend conventions; handle errors/validate inputs; document features; keep full stack coherent, clear, simple, beginner-friendly, and demonstrate best practices. Explain .NET Core/React concepts. Follow existing patterns when implementing workshop TODOs.
